A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GDPO work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison. The theoretical appendices and sample generations can be matched despite formatting changes and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original likelihood-estimation experiments on OpenWeb samples and GDPO fine-tuning results on mathematics, planning and coding benchmarks.

after.justification: v2 reports original GDPO results, including revised benchmark scores, computational-cost and quadrature-point ablations, and a coupled-GRPO comparison.

M1.justification: The SDMC estimator, sequence-level GDPO objective and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Using three instead of two quadrature points in the main mathematics/planning experiments changes the configuration of the existing method, rather than introducing a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions use OpenWeb for estimator analysis, GSM8K, MATH500, Countdown, 4x4 Sudoku, HumanEval and MBPP for evaluation, and KodCode-Light-RL-10K for coding fine-tuning. The added experiments reuse existing tasks; the new multimodality citation does not establish additional empirical coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds wD1 to the mathematics/planning comparisons previously containing LLaDA, diffu-GRPO and SFT plus diffu-GRPO. New Appendix E and Table 7 evaluate coupled-GRPO on Countdown and Sudoku. These additions materially broaden comparison with competing diffusion-policy optimization methods; the coding comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 2 changes from N=2 to N=3 quadrature points. The training table changes GPU counts from two to eight for GSM8K, Countdown and Sudoku, revises learning rates and selected-checkpoint iterations, and documents substantially different training configurations. Appendix D.2 adds a six-hour training-budget comparison. Figure 1 switches from the 256-token results to the best results across 128/256/512-token generations.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained Countdown estimator ablation in Figure 4, v2 adds a fixed-time computational-overhead study and an N=2 versus N=3 performance ablation on GSM8K and Countdown in Tables 4–5. Figure 3 also extends the SDMC analysis beyond five evaluations to eight. These additions substantially expand investigation of computational cost and quadrature sensitivity; the sample generations are retained, not newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions state 16 repetitions for likelihood estimation and retain Figure 2's mean-plus/minus-SD reporting. Figure 3 replaces shaded bands with asymmetric error bars without defining their bounds. The PDFs do not establish whether the statistical summary changed or only its numerical values and presentation. No new benchmark seed counts or significance tests are specified.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the main GDPO scores: for example, GSM8K at 512 tokens changes from 82.26 to 84.99 and Countdown from 66.41 to 80.86. These accompany changed quadrature and training settings, so they are not demonstrated same-setting gains. New Table 4 reports 4500, 3800 and 3500 iterations in six hours for diffu-GRPO, GDPO N=2 and GDPO N=3. Additional baseline and ablation results are reported, while Table 3's coding scores remain unchanged and Table 7 retains v1's planning GDPO scores.

T1.justification: The variance decomposition, asymptotic error bounds, assumptions, propositions and proofs in Appendices A–C are unchanged. Appendix E adds a mathematical explanation of an existing comparator, without revising GDPO's theoretical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statement and conclusion retain the same central claims: GDPO uses sequence-level ELBO estimation with SDMC to reduce variance efficiently and improve reasoning performance over pretrained checkpoints and competing methods. The new evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D.2 adds interpretation of the throughput cost of additional quadrature points and explicitly limits the timed experiment to iteration counts rather than accuracy. It also argues for N=3 as best overall, although Table 5 shows N=2 scoring higher on GSM8K at 128 and 256 tokens. Appendix E explains GDPO's distinct variance-reduction objective and flexible number of timesteps relative to coupled-GRPO.

D1.justification: The revised training table updates hardware, learning rates, quadrature counts and checkpoint metadata. The new studies disclose their time/batch settings and use of the official DiffuCoder implementation. Existing LoRA, AdamW, quantization, flash-attention and codebase information remains substantially unchanged, with no new code or data release documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Tang et al. on wD1, Shankar on PADRE, Huang et al. on diffusion-chain reasoning, and Venkatraman et al. on multimodal inference. New Appendix E expands the previously brief discussion of Gong et al.'s coupled-GRPO into an explicit comparison of objectives and timestep flexibility. The broader positioning of GDPO remains intact.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose remains substantively verbatim. Local edits update the introduction and experimental discussion. Appendix D is reorganized around rewards, ablations and training details; a comparison appendix is inserted, and the existing sample-generation appendix becomes Appendix F. Much apparent textual change comes from reflow rather than rewriting.

P2.justification: The visual evidence is substantially revised: Figure 1 changes its displayed summary and axes, Figure 3 replaces shaded bands with error bars, Table 2 gains a comparator row, and three experimental tables are added. The former final-page hyperparameter table moves into the training appendix as Table 6. Wider text areas and changed float placement reorganize presentation throughout the PDFs.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's limited comparator coverage and lack of timed overhead measurements, but introduces consequential reporting inconsistencies. Table 5's Countdown baseline reproduces MBPP values from Table 3 rather than the Countdown values in Table 2, and its diffu-GRPO row reproduces SFT-plus-diffu-GRPO scores. Table 6's eight-GPU configurations also conflict with the retained two-GPU efficiency statement. These problems undermine interpretation of the added evidence, leaving the net improvement in overall reliability uncertain despite useful comparisons and analyses.
